searchText: Weird, it worked perfectly for me guys, do we have forkchoice tests (for CL) for optimistic sync validation/invalidation (via latestValidHash) like we have in spec tests? or has any CL client has developed test vectors for validation/invalidation? or hive tests cover them up (just scraped through hive test repo on high level, but couldn't see how/where such testvectors are) There's an ongoing discussion about this. I myself would much rather have spectests about this, which are optional. This will require clients to mock an El and the testvectors include the El response. For Prysm this is very little to no work. And if other clients are in similar situations we would benefit a bit about this. There are situations that not only haven't been tested but we effectively know that we behave differently. merge-mock can easily mock EL and test vectors as far as my understanding of merge-mock is do you <@755590043632140352>/prysm have any test vectors documented ? even that would be awesome even if people can build their own forkchoice unit tests for those vectors i like the format of spec-tests, and could easily accommodate EL responses in it (as a step) (no need to set up EL) We have plenty of unit tests scattered in the forkchoice package dirs and some in the blockchain backage dirs, but none are well documented. But as you noticed, the issue here is more about the testvector formats. Even though Hive could probably take care of some of these situations. With spectest kind of testvectors, we could easily create crazy like forks that would be very hard on hive (I am assuming) and we can debug failures locally instead of relying on Mario pinging us. If Lodestar can accomodate this easily that makes now two of us. I suspect all clients have this one way or another. And already knowing that we would react the same way to an INVALID block that is some reassurance. yes, lodestar can easily accommodate this, so 👍 from our side if we can get them churned out
